issue.title: Walker footer clips off the window's left edge at narrow widths: freshnessFooterFit measures only its own item, not the status bar
issue.description:
Proposed by bob-cli-ra.5 (note #4, PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP) and triaged by the bob-cli-ra land agent.

## What is wrong

In a 420 px Obsidian window, the walker footer's status-bar content is cut off at the window's left edge. In the bob-cli-ra.5 acceptance captures (project, notebook, and prose notes, `n` family selected), the `[[ s w n b ]]` selector and the start of the links panel are cut. In `project-live-light-420.png` only part of the `s` letter shows, and the panel reads `⇄ Links · foo 2/3 open ⏮ pig ‹ bar bop › goo ⏭ · ]} goo`. The panel never sheds its hint, group arms, or context, because the fitter never sees an overflow.

## Root cause (confirmed by reading the code)

`freshnessFooterFit(el, parts, view)` in `plugins/bob-ledger-tools/src/121-freshness-footer-paint.js` (~line 484) sheds slots end-first in a loop guarded by `overflows()`, which returns only `el.scrollWidth > el.clientWidth + 1` (~line 604). The footer item is a flex child of Obsidian's right-anchored `.status-bar` and is not width-constrained, so its own `clientWidth` grows with its content and `overflows()` stays false. When the status bar as a whole is wider than the window, its left side overflows off-screen. All walker footers share this code (`s` review, `w` lane, `n` links, `b` bank), so the bug predates bob-cli-ra. The link-walk epic only made the `n` panel fuller on tree notes.

## Fix direction

Measure the space actually available to the footer item: for example, the status bar's `clientWidth` minus its siblings' widths, or the item's bounding rect against the status bar or window left edge. Feed that into the shed loop so slots shed end-first until the whole bar fits. Keep the shed order and calm states documented in `glossary:walker-footer` ("sheds end-first as the bar narrows"). Prove the fix in real Obsidian at 420 px for all four families (`scripts/obsidian-walker-footer-e2e.cjs` and `scripts/obsidian-tree-walk-e2e.cjs` both capture the status bar), and add a unit vector in which the parent bar overflows but the item does not.

Evidence: ra.5 screenshots `file:explicit:78352ade714018b409dcdcac` (run1/run2 `*-420.png`) and review `file:explicit:a1ed81b79efe17d52d0bc55e` ("Observations outside the rail").

task_type_fields.impact: At narrow widths (split panes, small laptop windows), every walker footer can lose its selector and leading context off-screen instead of shedding gracefully. That defeats the end-first shed contract, and the tree-note links panel is the most visible case.
task_type_fields.repro: Open a project, notebook, or prose note with the `n` bracket family selected in a 420 px-wide Obsidian window (the bob-cli-ra.5 tree-walk runner does this: `xvfb-run -a node scripts/obsidian-tree-walk-e2e.cjs` with the 420 px capture). The status bar's left side (the `[[ s w n b ]]` selector and the start of the Links panel) falls off the window's left edge, and no panel slot sheds.

issue.creation_reason: The bob-cli-ra link-walk acceptance found the walker footer clipped at 420 px. The defect is in the shared footer fitter that predates the epic, so it needs its own task rather than epic work.

payload.description: Same right-anchored status bar: the selector x shifts with panel width; a stable panel slot or width budget could fix both
Fixed narrow clipping of the cabinet pick overlay in the same footer at 420 px; reuse its shed and measure approach
